chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"It is not permissible for a woman to be married to her paternal uncle (from breastfeeding) nor her maternal uncle (from breastfeeding)."
ai.seo_question: Who are the uncles prohibited from marrying a woman due to breastfeeding?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies that the prohibition of marriage extends to the maternal and paternal uncles via breastfeeding (*radha'*), mirroring the status of direct ancestors. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that breastfeeding creates a permanent kinship bond (*mahramiyah*) comparable to blood relation, thereby preventing marriage even when the direct nursing mother is not involved. It highlights the precision of *fiqh* in distinguishing between consanguineous and affinal ties established through wet-nursing.
